The images on coins are one of the important categories of sources on this issue. As a genre of official art, usually with a portrait of the ruler, the coins convey the character’s attire in a realistic manner with details. The closest analogy to early Saka coins is imprinted with the image of a heavily armed rider. These are coins of Vanones, Azes, and Azilises (Fig. 7), and on certain types of Vanones’ coins, the horse is depicted in a protective armor. The bump on the horse’s body surface suggests that the protective apparel is not only for the rider but also for the horse.
